title: Seller Delta Cards — Compact Notes (draft)
body:
Purpose
---
Quick, scannable note set for sellers to handle questions about the latest inference runtime and routing changes (Feb 2025 release). Not a full battlecard — think 1-page pockets for SDRs/SEs during discovery and the first technical touch.

Why a separate "delta" set?
- Most sales interactions now hinge on what's changed vs competitor or customer status quo.
- We need micro-narratives: cost delta, latency delta, operational delta.
- Short, action-first prompts sellers can memorize.

TL;DR (30s scripts)
- Executive: "We help you run LLM inference with predictable latency and 30–45% lower token cost on typical chat workloads by combining smart batching, prefix cache, and dynamic routing across cheaper model variants."
- Platform/infra buyer: "You get a single runtime that can fallback to cheaper variants automatically and provide per-route SLOs — so P95 latency and cost are uncoupled for most request patterns."
- Developer: "Same API, fewer surprises — local dev -> hosted -> private, identical telemetry and a dev-mode that simulates routing policies."

Delta Signals (what changed in Feb release)
- Dynamic routing policy (beta): route by policy priority (latency -> cost -> region). Sellers: emphasize pluggable rules instead of one-size-fits-all.
- KV prefix cache upgrade: hot prefixes served from RAM, reducing token-generation by 10–25% on repeat queries.
- New optimized kernels for 2k-seq models on A10X: P99 drop by ~18ms in internal tests.
- Billing meter tweak: per-response prefix cache hits now accounted separately (shows up as "cache credits" on invoice).

Key buyer objections + suggested reactions (short)
- "We can run these models ourselves on prem cheaper." -> "Totally — for steady-state throughput you might. Where customers gain is predictable ops (SLAs, rollouts, fallbacks) and the cost of engineering time to replicate safe routing, fallback logic, and observability. We can hand over private with the same controls. (see pilot offer below)"
- "We need data residency/air-gapped support." -> "Private deployment is available; common ask is onboarding and KMS integration — we offer an on-prem package + professional services to shorten that ramp. Quick checklist: KMS, VPC peering, audit logs. I can loop in Solutions Eng."
- "How do you handle model regressions?" -> "We recommend prompt-anchored evals + split traffic rollouts; our Console surfaces drift and can auto-roll back to a pinned variant if QA fails. (Link eval IDE)"

Top 3 sales hooks (by persona)
- Platform Architect: "Predictable tail latency and explicit fallbacks — fewer incidents during traffic spikes."
- Product Manager: "Lower per-interaction cost and consistent UX during scale — so your product metrics don't degrade as usage grows."
- Developer/Integrator: "Same SDK and local dev mode so your CI can validate responses before hitting production."

Micro-technical checklist (one-liners sellers can ask/record)
- Expected QPS and median seq length?
- Current model(s) in use + any quantized variants?
- SLO expectations (P50/P95/P99) and acceptable cost/cpm tradeoff?
- Existing caching/batching patterns? Are there heavy repeated prefixes (search snippets, templated prompts)?
- Any regulatory constraints (SOC2, HIPAA, RoPA)?

Pilot offer (compact)
- 4-week pilot: reserved dev-capacity + routing-policy proof-of-concept. Deliverables: configured routing rules, prefix cache report, baseline v. optimized cost delta, and a short ops playbook.
- Success criteria: 20–30% cost reduction on tracked flows OR P99 latency within agreed threshold + integration of 1 rollback policy.
- Pricing: waived onboarding for pilot if we get PO for dedicated capacity conversion within 90 days (negotiable).

Mini case vignette (one-liner evidence)
- "MarketFeed (ad-tech) cut per-article generation cost by 28% using routing + cache; kept tail latency under 150ms for 95% of traffic during a campaign spike."

Slide / demo notes for 3-slide drop-in (for SEs)
1) Problem: unpredictable tail and rising token spend as usage grows — show small table: baseline cost vs expected growth.
2) Our delta: what changed — 3 bullets (routing, cache, kernels) + simple graph: cost vs latency.
3) Pilot ask + CTA: 4-week pilot bullets + next steps.

Rapid rebuttal snippets (copy-paste for Slack/Email)
- "If ops is a concern, we can run a short safety audit and propose a migration with staging fallbacks — usually 2 weeks to validate."
- "We log per-token costs and cache hit rates; we can share an anonymized sample dashboard as part of discovery."

Questions we still have / things to finalize
- Confirm exact invoicing label for "cache credits" (finance/contact: Priya) so sellers can explain billing.
- Final wording for private deployment SLA for Feb patch (legal review pending).
- Collect 2 more micro-case studies outside ad-tech — ideally one fintech and one enterprise SaaS.

Notes to self (informal)
- Pull internal perf deck w/ A10X numbers (Julian).
- Add short script for SE to show Console demo: filter by route -> show rollouts -> demonstrate rollback.
- Remove any heavy technical jargon on the final pocket card; keep 1-liners.

Next steps / owners
- Anika: finalize seller pocket and hand to SE kit (end of week).
- Julian: provide kernel perf slides + one graph (2 days).
- Priya: confirm billing label with finance (3 days).

Slack refs / tickets
- #se-enablement (thread pinned: Feb release delta notes)
- JIRA: JIRA-INFER-842 (routing policy rollout)

Todo (short)
- [ ] Create printable 3x5 "delta card" PDF for SEs (Anika)
- [ ] Draft short email template to ops/infra buyer (Julian)
- [ ] Capture pilot PO template & legal checklist (Priya)

End notes
- Keep iteration frequency high — this doc is meant to change as field feedback arrives. If an SE flags a missing rebuttal or case study, add it to the card immediately and push a short changelog to #se-enablement.

(rough draft; intended to be condensed into a single-slide pocket or two-sided PDF for quick printing)
